newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P sees further Thai financial woes but no crisis.
newsitem.headline: S&P sees further Thai financial woes but no crisis.

text.p: The creditworthiness of Thailand's financial institutions could come under further pressure but the stress on the sector is unlikely to reach crisis proportions, Standard and Poor's Corp said in a report released on Tuesday.
S&P said it believes, however, that the government of Thailand has ample resources to cope with potential sector losses.

Tight monetary policies and the property market slump in an environment of lax prudential regulatory requirements, declining margins, and rising corporate and household indebtedness have weakened loan portfolios and, along with them, the average credit quality of the financial sector, S&P said in the report.
On March 18, 1997, S&P affirmed the Kingdom of Thailand's Single-A long-term rating and A-1 short-term foreign currency ratings. It said the country's long-term ratings outlook remains stable.
The report released Tuesday, entitled "Thailand: Sovereign Unscathed by Financial Sector Stress" details S&P's previously released views on Thailand.
